items.title: Lemon Nash Interview, 1961-06-20
items.q: Well, I do know Lou Armstrong played up there once.

ctx.x: Do you remember what bands played in there?

What bands played up there? Yeah, I'll tell you what bands played up there. Well, I do know Lou Armstrong played up there once. I remember Louie played up there once. After he went away and got so famous, he's played up there since he's been famous. But now I'm trying to think of the other guys that played up there. This fellow Peter William, he played up there. He's a drummer, Dixieland musician. Peter William and his band played up there. Drums, piano, bass, violin, tenor, banjo. This fellow Guy E, the one who…
I know he'd get a kick out of that.

items.title: Lemon Nash Interview, 1959-10-03
items.q: But Papa Celestine and Lou Armstrong, about the oldest two bands that I know around here.

ctx.x: Do you remember any of the other guys? Huh? Who were some of the other early musicians you remember?

Well, after that then Sam Morgan. I mean Celestine was about the only best band that I could really remember around here, Papa Celestine. And then after Papa Celestine then it was Sam Morgan. After Sam Morgan then Chris Kelly had a band. After Chris Kelly then it was Buddy P.T. He had a band, played a trumpet. After Buddy P.T. then Kid Ran A. He up with a band. But Papa Celestine and Lou Armstrong, about the oldest two bands that I know around here. That's right, Papa Celestine and Lou Armstrong.
Well did you hear many guys walking around serenading? Oh yeah, yeah.
